data.ruling: The refutation stands. V113 asks for the lowest voltage at the servo converter's VIN when it runs from the pack. It asks whether that is 6.0 V, or 6.0 V less a stated drop across the pack path. The value gives 6.0 V at the pack terminals and says the drop across R5's pack path is not read. The owner's V294 answer of 2026-10-02 states the pack-path sizing that the value itself cites: "The pack path stays sized at 6.0 V: 52.1 A nominal at a 5.8 V bus, rated 60 A". The 52.1 A comes from FU-2B1's R5 P2 V90 value, 302.0 W in at a 5.8 V bus (302.0 / 5.8 = 52.07 A). That 302.0 W includes the four TPS55285 inputs (283.7 W). The bus is therefore the node at the converters' VIN, and the owner's sizing puts it at 5.8 V. That is 0.2 V under the 6.0 V pack floor. A stated figure for the drop exists in an owner answer, so the value is wrong to say it is not read. It is also wrong to check the converter from 6.0 V and not from 5.8 V. The rest of the value is right: 6.0 V at the pack terminals (IOBoard.md Pack voltage range) and the 6.6 V under-load floor (V294). The TPS55285 still runs at 5.8 V: SLVSI72A 5.2 gives a VIN range of 2.4 to 22 V for VOUT of 3.0 V or more. The 5.8 V figure changes the low-end input and inductor currents R6 checks, not whether the part is usable. The finding concerns this function's requirement value, not the part.
